newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM names cabinet with veteran in finance post.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM names cabinet with veteran in finance post.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto named a new cabinet on Thursday, appointing a 69-year-old veteran politician, Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, as the country's finance minister.
The 20-member cabinet included only one woman and only two ministers, including Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, retained their posts from the previous cabinet.

The key Finance Ministry post went to Hiroshi Mitsuzuka, who will have the tough job of presiding over a planned break-up of the powerful ministry, following scandals involving top bureaucrats and alleged mishandling of problems at financial institutions.

Mitsuzuka was responsible for the privatisation of the near-bankrupt Japan National Railways in the 1980s. He is a former trade minister and leads one of the biggest factions in Hashimoto's ruling Liberal Democratic Party.
Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama, 70, retained his post, continuing his role as the government's top spokesman.
The only woman in the cabinet is Environment Minister Michiko Ishii, 63, a pharmacist known for her work in the fields of medicine and welfare.
